text:
A: Hello. Another one.
B: Hello. Yes, I think this is the last. I'm Helen.
A: Shahida. Ilford. Five calls, I didn't know it is five.
B: Nor did I, to be honest. I'm in Otley, near Leeds.
A: You have many books. In your picture. You are teacher?
B: Erm, no, not quite. Archivist. I look after old papers at a university library. Letters, diaries.
A: Old letters. People pay for this?
B: Not very much. But yes. Someone has to make sure they don't get thrown away. Otherwise in fifty years nobody knows what happened.
A: Hm. My mother's letters from Lahore, I still have them. In a box, in the wardrobe.
B: Do you? I'd keep them dry. And not in plastic, if you can help it, it makes them sweat.
A: Ok. I didn't know. My daughter says throw old things, I say no.
B: I'm on your side there.
A: You have children?
B: A daughter, Isla. She's nine.
A: Husband?
B: No. We weren't married. Her dad's in Bradford, she goes to him every other weekend. It works, mostly. And my mum helps, she does the Tuesday pick-up.
A: Good. Grandmother is important. I do my son's children, two days. Seven and five. I give them dinner, I check homework. Their mother is busy.
B: My mum would say the same about me, probably.
A: Your mum is right. Mothers are usually right.
B: She wants to get a dog at the moment. She's seventy. I've told her it'll be me walking it.
A: Of course it will be you. My husband wanted a dog once. I said who cleans? He went quiet.
B: That's a good question to ask, actually. I might borrow it.
A: Borrow, ok. What you eat for dinner, with your daughter?
B: Erm, simple things. Lentil soup, pasta. I'm usually too tired by six to do much. I bake bread at the weekend, though.
A: Lentils is good. Daal is lentils. Put cumin, garlic, little chilli for you, not too much for child.
B: I'll try that. Isla likes things plain, so it'll be a negotiation.
A: Children must eat what you make. That's it.
B: You'd do well in our house.
A: Everybody says. You walk a lot? You look thin.
B: I walk up the Chevin most Sundays, the hill by the town. Early, before anyone's about.
A: Alone? Be careful.
B: I will. There's mostly just a heron and the odd dog walker.
A: Acha. I think now time is finishing. Bas.
B: Yes. Thank you, it was nice to talk.
